subject: rstan too-many-dlls problem - are there sane solutions?

messages.author: 3e64c3dd638b246a
messages.subject: rstan too-many-dlls problem - are there sane solutions?
parts:
Dear all,


I'm trying to run sensitivity analyses (e.g. hundreds of fits with varying priors). If I understand correctly, if the prior changes I DO need to recompile the model, so updating is not an option.

As has been pointed out, cleaning up the dll's would be desirable as default R has a dll maximum of 100: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24832030/exceeded-maximum-number-of-dlls-in-r

I have tried the solution by Frederic H. (last reply on the page) but this unpredictably and repeatedly crashes my rsession, at least if I run multiple instances of R.

My question is: are there any plans to include dll cleanup or even sensitivity analysis functions in rstan in the future and do you have any suggestions for how I could avoid 100+ dll's piling up?

I should mention that I run rstan via the brms package on Windows 7, using R64 & RStudio.


Regards and thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan too-many-dlls problem - are there sane solutions?
parts:
On Monday, November 21, 2016 at 5:44:04 AM UTC-5, Paul Zerr wrote:
I'm trying to run sensitivity analyses (e.g. hundreds of fits with varying priors). If I understand correctly, if the prior changes I DO need to recompile the model, so updating is not an option.
Hundreds of prior families or just different hyperparameter values? If the later, then you should be able to pass those values into the data block and not recompile.
My question is: are there any plans to include dll cleanup or even sensitivity analysis functions in rstan in the future and do you have any suggestions for how I could avoid 100+ dll's piling up?

No plans to remove the dlls (they are needed for some post-estimation functions). You could call Stan (via brm) in a separate R processes using the makePSOCKcluster() function in the parallel library and then kill that process with stopCluster(). But you would need to avoid returning an object to the parent process that contains the stanfit object, possibly by calling as.array() or something.

Ben
